To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed an efficient method to track the beating heart in 2D and 3D, based on a TPS model for the heart deformation, that is able to handle arbitrary illumination changes and large deformations.
we propose a new framework for the tracking of the heart in minimally invasive surgery.

we propose an efficient algorithm for tracking the heart motion in 3D, based on a thin-plate spline parametric model for surface deformation, that can be used for compensation of the heart surface motion in robotic-assisted minimallly invasive surgery.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a vision based system to compensate the motion of the heart surface during cardiac MIS.
the development of a novel method for heart motion tracking that is capable of dealing with large non-rigid motion, illumination variations and 3D deformations.
the development of a robust and accurate method to track and compensate for the heart motion, in order to enable the design of a vision-based motion compensation system for MIS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed algorithm is a promising approach for tracking the heart motion in MIS, which is able to cope with the challenging conditions of the MIS environment.

the presented method is a robust and efficient solution to the problem of tracking the motion of the heart surface, and can be used in real-time to enable motion compensation for robotic-assisted MIS.
our method provides the best tracking performance among all the methods that we have compared to, both in 2D and 3D, and in terms of accuracy and robustness.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we present a new framework for tracking the heart motion that is able to cope with large non-rigid motion, illumination changes and occlusions, and is robust to the initial estimation of the heart shape.
the proposed framework is capable of tracking the surface motion of the heart, even under severe non-rigid deformities and large illumination changes.

the proposed framework is able to track the heart surface with high precision and robustness under arbitrary lighting conditions, even for large non-rigid motions and in the presence of specular reflections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed method can be used for the design of motion compensation systems for MIS cardiac robotic-assisted surgery, which is a very challenging task.
the proposed framework can be used to efficiently track the motion of the heart surface in a real-time manner and thus, it can be used for real-time motion compensation in cardiac robotic-assist MIS.
the proposed method can provide a robust and efficient solution to the heart surface tracking problem.
